steps.what: Review the robotics project work, technical responsibilities and actual unresolved integration issues in {PROJECT}
Supervise technologists, technicians and engineers, review actual technical work and discuss constraints and next actions
Write and check the actual technical instructions and unresolved decisions in existing {PROJECT} items
Post the exact checked technical updates in {PROJECT}

tasks.design: Keep technical supervision and actual instruction capture in existing {PROJECT} items. After separating the written work and posting, no duplicate entry or safe substitute for supervision is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision depends on actual technical work and the staff's questions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project records already support direct instruction entry; no further mechanism is established.
tasks.still_hard: Cross-domain problems and responsibility for technical decisions need a person.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer knows when a team member needs clarification or specialist help.

ambition.what: No automated staff assessment or allocation.

reach.learn: Connect observed robot behaviour to the engineering work item.

evidence.claim: Technical supervision requires interpreting actual work and responding to staff questions.

assumptions: Boundary is technical supervision and ordinary work-item direction, excluding other staff's execution and employment performance decisions.

Project owners supply actual item ID, responsibility, revision and unresolved issue. The engineer checks these in s1, discusses real work in s2 and writes instructions in s3. Missing context is clarified manually; no free meeting extraction is assumed.

Illustrative shares are unmeasured. Existing native entry is assumed, with no duplicate capture established. The ordinary final s3 check binds completed instructions before posting. No new tool means zero upkeep.
unknowns: Whether actual direction is entered directly in native work items
research_questions: Is any confirmed duplicate technical record capture present?

already_counted.description: Actual written technical direction and checking remain in s3.

incremental.description: No new tool or procedure; zero additional upkeep.

approvals.approved_version: Completed technical updates checked in s3; edits void the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Work review, live supervision, actual instructions and posting are split and unchanged. No administrative baseline or automated supervision benefit is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define the manufacturing robot's application, interfaces, timing, failure handling and boundary to independently engineered safety functions
Design software architecture to control the robotic system, selecting state handling, data flow and interface contracts before writing implementation code
Draft non-safety device-adapter code in the software-engineering category of {OTHER}, first reusing native blocks and using bounded code suggestions only for the remaining varying interface glue

loop.purpose: Draft a narrowly scoped non-safety device adapter from a checked interface contract.
loop.input: Checked architecture, exact device API pages, typed interface contract and existing tests.
loop.output: Proposed adapter diff with source API references, no deployment capability.
loop.check: The engineer checks semantic units, state transitions, timeout and error behaviour against requirements and API text; compilation, unit tests and the later integration tests also run. Executable code alone is insufficient.
loop.stop: One suggested diff and at most one correction; unsupported API, failed checks or unresolved behaviour goes to manual coding.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native control blocks and templates are tested first. A bounded reader can help only where varying device API text leaves genuine custom glue; fixed interfaces use deterministic templates instead.

steps.what: Review and test the complete control code in isolated simulation or a controlled test setup, checking intended behaviour, limits and failures; write test findings and check the final code snapshot
Commit the exact checked robot-software snapshot to the controlled source-record category of {OTHER}

tasks.design: Test native control blocks before any custom code. For residual device adapters, a bounded model in the software-engineering category of {OTHER} proposes a diff from exact API sources; the engineer checks meaning and tests the complete software before committing its final version, with no live deployment action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different device APIs can require custom adapter glue despite reusable architecture.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded source-grounded code suggestions can reduce drafting when their full review and tests are retained.
tasks.still_hard: Concurrency, physical assumptions and failure handling can be wrong despite passing narrow tests.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer determines whether software behaviour satisfies the actual robot application.

ambition.what: No autonomous robot operation, deployment or safety-function change.

tasks.altitude: Less residual glue drafting if review costs allow, unchanged control design authority.

reach.learn: Translate an API claim into a controlled physical test.

evidence.claim: Bounded code suggestions may assist device-adapter drafting, but behaviour, API grounding and integration still need full engineering checks.

assumptions: Boundary is offline design and development for manufacturing, through a versioned code design. Production deployment and safety-control engineering remain separate authorised work and earn no saving.

The application owner supplies requirements; device sources supply exact API revision, types, units, timing and error behaviour. The engineer captures and checks the contract in s1-s2 and supplies source pages in s3. Missing documentation causes manual coding or clarification; no guessed API or free structured contract is assumed.

Native blocks first. Shares are an illustrative custom-adapter scenario, not measured baseline. Code review is counted in s3 and complete testing in s4; runtime earns no saving. Final s4 checking binds exact code and test snapshot before commit; edits invalidate it.
unknowns: Whether native blocks already cover all interfaces
Whether code review costs outweigh draft reduction
research_questions: Does one real adapter diff save drafting time after semantic review and failed suggestions?

already_counted.description: Code semantic review and full final integration testing remain in s3-s4.

incremental.description: Maintain adapter prompts, API source versions and regression tests after device changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact code diff and complete test findings checked in s4; edits require rechecking and retesting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Residual adapter drafting saves 10.5 gross hours less 2.5 upkeep for 8 net in a successful bounded-assistance scenario. Native coverage or review-heavy code gives zero benefit; architecture, tests and commit retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Locate technical papers and prior system evidence for a stated robotic capability using native topic, author and date filters in {DOCS}
Read and assess robotics evidence, compare assumptions and define the research hypothesis and evaluation criteria
Conduct research on robotic technology by developing and testing a prototype or controlled simulation for the new system capability and capturing actual failures and results
Interpret actual research results and write and check the completed capability finding and its limits in {DOCS}
Save the exact checked robotics research note in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native research-archive filters in {DOCS} to shorten source navigation. Keep reading, hypothesis selection, controlled prototype or simulation work in the robotics-research category of {OTHER} and interpretation human, then save the checked actual finding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant prior capability studies can be hard to locate in an archive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing source metadata can narrow navigation without synthesising conclusions.
tasks.still_hard: A published capability may depend on assumptions that fail in the intended application.
tasks.human_edge: The researcher distinguishes a demonstration from a general capability claim.

ambition.what: No new production capability is assumed before research succeeds.

tasks.altitude: Less source navigation, unchanged research judgement.

reach.learn: Check how hardware limitations affect a capability claim.

evidence.claim: Source filters can shorten archive navigation without replacing reading or robotics research.

assumptions: Boundary is exploratory capability research, separate from application control-software design in 16528. Actual prototype and simulation work is retained, with no deployment or runtime saving.

The archive supplies title, author, date, topic and source location. The engineer checks relevance in s1, reads and defines the hypothesis in s2 and captures actual case, condition, result and failure in s3. Missing metadata requires manual search; no free structured research finding is assumed.
Native filters first; illustrative shares are unmeasured. Final s4 checking follows completed actual evidence and wording; edits void the save gate.
unknowns: Whether archive filters already remove navigation work
research_questions: What repeated source search remains after native filtering?

already_counted.description: Source relevance review remains in s1.

incremental.description: Maintain saved searches and source metadata.

approvals.approved_version: Completed actual research note checked in s4; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Archive navigation saves 4.5 gross hours less 1 upkeep for 3.5 net. Already usable filters give zero gain. Reading, research, interpretation and save retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate robot mechanical failures and maintenance problems

steps.what: Inspect the failed robotic mechanism in a safe state, examine wear, alignment and damage and capture actual observations
Collect and verify actual robot event, service and operating-load records in the maintenance-record category of {OTHER}
Align timestamps and plot explicit load and event series in the engineering-analysis category of {OTHER}, using native views without inferring causation
Investigate mechanical failure hypotheses and unexpected maintenance causes against actual evidence and controlled checks
Write and check the completed failure finding, evidence, uncertainty and recommended next work in {DOCS}
Save the exact checked failure report in {DOCS}

tasks.design: Test native timestamp alignment and trend views in the engineering-analysis category of {OTHER}. Keep physical inspection, data verification and causal investigation human, then check and save the completed failure report with unresolved uncertainty visible.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event and load plots can be assembled repeatedly by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views can reuse explicit time and signal mappings.
tasks.still_hard: A coincident event does not establish a mechanical failure cause.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer relates physical wear and operating evidence to testable failure hypotheses.

ambition.what: No autonomous maintenance instruction or robot restart.

tasks.altitude: Less timeline setup, unchanged causal judgement.

reach.task: Explain physical wear and maintenance history
reach.learn: Preserve actual evidence before parts are disturbed.

evidence.claim: Native time-series views can reduce repeated plot setup without establishing failure causation.

assumptions: Boundary is investigation and a saved finding, excluding repair, restart and other-role maintenance work.

The engineer captures physical observations in s1 and verifies equipment ID, timestamp, clock offset, signal, unit, service action and provenance in s2. Existing maintenance records supply raw events, not a free cleaned timeline. Missing data are investigated manually; uncertain timing stays flagged.
Native configuration first. Shares are illustrative and unmeasured. Final s5 checking follows completed report wording and evidence; edits invalidate its save gate.
unknowns: Whether event and load views already align natively
research_questions: How much actual timeline assembly remains beyond existing views?

incremental.description: Maintain signal and timestamp mappings after controller changes.

approvals.approved_version: Final failure report and actual evidence checked in s5; edits require rechecking.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Repeated timeline setup saves 6 gross hours less 1 upkeep for 5 net. Existing native views give zero gain. Inspection, data capture, causal testing and save retain effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Residual adapter drafting and evidence setup may shrink; supervision, research and physical failure judgement remain human.
reach: Coordinate with robotics technicians, mechatronics engineers and mechanics.
role.ambitious_version: A robotics engineer who keeps proposed code and causal claims tied to exact interfaces and actual tests.
